searches.note: Twenty three searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h2, none of them the author's; five left unspent. Five were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain and read through their summaries: maisons-champagne.com with champagne-deutz.com (the chronology), champagne-deutz.com (the philosophy page, the vats), champagne-drappier.com twice (the Charles de Gaulle sheet and the history page; the Grande Sendrée sheets) and one with dreyfusashby.com. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries.

tested.founded: 1859 at Vertus: the house, the union, Wikipedia, Hameau Albert. The founders' trades: Duval a grower and maker of Vertus, Leroy a wine trader of Villers-Franqueux (Wikipedia, Hameau Albert); the record had two merchants. One merchant's marriage of 1859 is not taught.
tested.story: The head of the house died in 1991 and his widow led it from that year: Wikipedia, Hameau Albert, a trade profile. The widow married into the family. The two firsts are the house's own claims: the organic Brut is supported by merchants too, the High Environmental Value first is 'one of the first' elsewhere, so it stays told as the house's claim.
tested.cuvee: First vintage 1990: Tastingbook, Champagne Club, Wikipedia; release 1999 in one profile, 1996 in another, left out. 2002: 95 per cent Chardonnay of Avize, Cramant, Oger and Le Mesnil with Pinot Noir of Ambonnay, Brut Nature, about a fifth in barrels of 220 litres (the house's sheet, Decanter, merchants). 2004: 87 and 13 by Gault et Millau, consistent with the blend in words.
tested.forms: Femme de Champagne Grand Cru Brut, a non vintage, confirmed by Falstaff, World of Fine Wine and vino.com.
tested.people: The widow, the cellar master and the sons are living and never named.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: sound.

changes.was: two families of the wine trade; a merchant of Vertus named Duval
changes.now: a family of Vertus and a wine trading family of Villers-Franqueux; a Duval of Vertus and a Leroy, a wine trader of Villers-Franqueux
changes.why: Duval was a grower and maker, not a merchant, by two sources.

changes.was: his widow, a descendant of the founders by marriage
changes.now: his widow, who had married into the founding family
changes.why: One does not descend by marriage.

changes.was: the Clos des Bouveries above the village
changes.now: the Clos des Bouveries at Vertus
changes.why: Above the village had no source.
sources: Gault et Millau: Clos des Bouveries

changes.was: one of the few large houses based in the Côte des Blancs rather than at Reims or Épernay
changes.now: cut from the story; the answer says most houses on the class sheet stand at Reims or Épernay instead
changes.why: A comparative of size with no source; the sheet's own roster shows the second.

changes.was: a part of them is fermented in oak barrels, the share moving by vintage, by critics' notes
changes.now: the same, with about a fifth of the 2002 in barrels of 220 litres by the house's sheet
changes.why: The house's own figure for one vintage.
sources: Champagne Duval-Leroy: Femme de Champagne technical sheet

changes.was: Union des Maisons de Champagne: Maison Duval-Leroy
changes.now: Champagne Duval-Leroy: Femme de Champagne technical sheet
changes.why: Ten is the cap; the union's chronology still stands for 1857 and 1859.

changes.was: with a little Pinot Noir from Ambonnay
changes.now: with a little Grand Cru Pinot Noir from the Montagne de Reims
changes.why: The spoken line told one vintage's village as the wine's rule; the record's own sites field gives Ambonnay for the 2002 and the Montagne de Reims for later vintages.
sources: Duval-Leroy: Femme de Champagne Brut technical sheet

open: The release of the 1990 Femme: one profile gives 1999, another 1996; still left out.
The house's rule of ten years at least for Femme was seen in one summary only and is not taught.
